REST API for managing public assistance applications. Covers the full intake lifecycle: applications, household members, household data, income, jobs, assets, expenses, health plans, health enrollments, contacts, organizations, person relationships, authorized representatives, tax filers, sponsors, signatures, verifications, and interviews.

Status: Alpha — Breaking changes expected.

Applications

Manage public assistance applications.

▶ GET /applications List applications listApplications #

Retrieve a paginated list of applications.

Returns ApplicationList

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

Members

Household members included in an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/members List application members listApplicationMembers #

Retrieve all household members linked to this application.

Returns ApplicationMemberList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

Responses

A paginated list of application members. ApplicationMemberList application/json

hasNext boolean

▶ retroactiveMedicalCoverage RetroactiveMedicalCoverage { isRequested, periods } Retroactive Medicaid coverage request for a household member. Medicaid may cover medical expenses incurred up to 3 months before the application date if the member would have been eligible (42 CFR § 435.914).

isDisabled boolean
Whether the member has a disability as defined by the applying program.
hasLongTermCondition boolean

institutionType enum

Whether the member is fleeing prosecution, custody, or confinement for a felony. Disqualifies from SNAP (7 CFR § 273.11(n)) and TANF (45 CFR § 261.55).

Whether the member has a state or federal drug-related felony conviction. States may apply a lifetime ban or modified rules under 21 U.S.C. § 862a.
convictedDuplicateSnapBenefits boolean
Whether the member has been convicted of fraudulently obtaining SNAP benefits in multiple jurisdictions simultaneously (7 CFR § 273.11(c)).
convictedOfSnapTrafficking boolean
Whether the member has been convicted of SNAP benefit trafficking. Permanent disqualification (7 CFR § 273.11(b)).
convictedTradingSnapForFirearmsOrExplosives boolean
Whether the member has been convicted of trading SNAP benefits for firearms, ammunition, or explosives. Permanent disqualification (7 CFR § 273.11(b)).
convictedOfDisqualifyingViolentCrime boolean
Whether the member has a conviction for a disqualifying violent crime under state law.
disqualifiedForIPV boolean
Whether the member has been disqualified for an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) under 7 CFR § 273.16.
isViolatingProbationOrParole boolean
Whether the member is in violation of a condition of probation or parole. Disqualifies from SNAP (7 CFR § 273.11(n)).

Whether the member is requesting retroactive Medicaid coverage.

The month for which coverage is requested, in YYYY-MM format.
householdIncome number · float
Total household income for this month. Used to assess eligibility for the retroactive period.
▶ disability Disability { hasLongTermCondition, hasMentalDisability, hasPhysicalDisability, +2 } Disability status for a household member. Affects SNAP medical expense deductions for elderly or disabled members (7 CFR § 273.9(d)(3)), TANF exemptions from work requirements, and Medicaid disability pathways.
isDisabled boolean
Whether the member has a disability as defined by the applying program.
hasLongTermCondition boolean
Whether the disability or health condition is expected to last 12 months or more.
hasPhysicalDisability boolean
Whether the member has a physical disability.
hasMentalDisability boolean
Whether the member has a mental health condition or intellectual disability.
needsHelpWithSelfCare boolean
Whether the member needs assistance with activities of daily living.
▶ studentStatus StudentStatus { enrollmentStatus, institutionType, isParticipatingInWorkStudy, +1 } Student enrollment information for a household member. institutionType enum

▶ fosterCare FosterCare { endDate, exitReason, exitState, +4 } Foster care history for a household member. Young adults who aged out of foster care may qualify for Medicaid coverage up to age 26 regardless of income under the Fostering Connections Act (42 U.S.C. § 675a).

Tax Filers

Tax filing status records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/tax-filers List tax filers listTaxFilers #

Retrieve tax filer records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns TaxFilerList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

memberId string · uuid

Filter records by the household member they belong to.

Health Plans

Health coverage plan records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/health-plans List health plans listHealthPlans #

Retrieve health plan records for an application.

Returns HealthPlanList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

Responses

A paginated list of health plan records. HealthPlanList application/json
total integer required
Total number of items available.
limit integer required
Maximum number of items requested.
offset integer required
Number of items skipped before the current page.
hasNext boolean
Whether more items are available beyond the current page.

Health Enrollments

Member enrollment records linking household members to health plans.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/health-enrollments List health enrollments listHealthEnrollments #

Retrieve health enrollment records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns HealthEnrollmentList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

memberId string · uuid

Filter records by the household member they belong to.

hasNext boolean
Whether more items are available beyond the current page.

Contacts

Non-member contact records for an application (authorized representatives, sponsors, tax dependents, etc.).

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/contacts List contacts listContacts #

Retrieve non-member contact records for an application.

Returns ContactList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

Person Relationships

Directional relationship records between any two persons in an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/person-relationships List person relationships listPersonRelationships #

Retrieve person relationship records for an application.

Returns PersonRelationshipList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

Number of items skipped before the current page.
hasNext boolean
Whether more items are available beyond the current page.

Signatures

Signature records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/signatures List signatures listSignatures #

Retrieve signature records for an application.

Returns SignatureList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

Jobs

Employment records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/jobs List jobs listJobs #

Retrieve job records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns JobList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/incomes List income listIncome #

Retrieve income records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns IncomeList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

memberId string · uuid

Filter records by the household member they belong to.

Responses

A paginated list of income records. IncomeList application/json
total integer required
Total number of items available.
limit integer required
Maximum number of items requested.
offset integer required
Number of items skipped before the current page.
hasNext boolean
Whether more items are available beyond the current page.

Assets

Asset records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/assets List assets listAssets #

Retrieve asset records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns AssetList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

Asset Disposals

Asset disposal records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/asset-disposals List asset disposals listAssetDisposals #

Retrieve asset disposal records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns AssetDisposalList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Expenses

Expense records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/expenses List expenses listExpenses #

Retrieve expense records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns ExpenseList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

"%22
:%3A

<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt

A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

Deductions

Above-the-line tax deduction records for an application.

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/deductions List deductions listDeductions #

Retrieve deduction records for an application. Filter by memberId to scope to a single member.

Returns DeductionList

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Review

▶ GET /applications/{applicationId}/review/demographics Get applicationReview demographics section panel getApplicationReviewDemographicsSection #
Returns ApplicationReviewSectionResponse

Path parameters

applicationId string · uuid required

Unique identifier of the application.

Query parameters

q string

Search query using field:value syntax. Multiple conditions separated by spaces are ANDed together.

More

Examples

  • john — exact match for "john" in searchable fields
  • *john* — contains "john" in searchable fields
  • name:*smith* — name contains "smith" (case-insensitive)
  • email:*@example.com — email ends with "@example.com"
  • status:approved — exact match on status field
  • status:approved,pending — status is "approved" OR "pending"
  • income:>=1000 — income greater than or equal to 1000
  • created:>2024-01-01 — created after January 1, 2024
  • status:approved income:>=1000 — approved AND income >= 1000 (multiple conditions)
  • -status:denied — exclude records with status "denied"
  • -deletedAt:* — only records where deletedAt does not exist

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
termFull-text exact matchjohn
*term*Full-text contains*john*
term*Full-text starts withjohn*
*termFull-text ends with*smith
field:valueExact match on fieldstatus:approved
field:*value*Contains (case-insensitive)name:*john*
field:value*Starts withname:john*
field:*valueEnds withemail:*@example.com
field:"value"Quoted value (for spaces)name:"john doe"
field.nested:valueNested field (dot notation)address.state:CA
field:>valueGreater thanincome:>1000
field:>=valueGreater than or equalincome:>=1000
field:<valueLess thanincome:<5000
field:<=valueLess than or equalincome:<=5000
field:val1,val2Match any value (OR)status:approved,pending
-field:valueExclude / negate-status:denied
field:*Field exists (not null)email:*
-field:*Field does not exist-deletedAt:*

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

URL Encoding Reference

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

CharacterEncoded
(space)%20 or +
"%22
:%3A
>%3E
<%3C
,%2C

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

limit integer

Maximum number of items to return (1-100).

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Syntax

PatternDescriptionExample
fieldNameAscendingsort=createdAt
-fieldNameDescendingsort=-createdAt
field1,field2Multi-fieldsort=status,-priority
nested.fieldNested field via dot notationsort=name.lastName

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples above show human-readable syntax for clarity.

Lists

A condition on a list matches when any item matches. That holds for a list of values (programs:snap) and for a list of objects anywhere along a dotted path (members.firstName:Jo, any member named Jo).

Each condition is checked on its own. members.firstName:Jo members.age:>60 matches when some member is named Jo and some member, not necessarily the same one, is over 60. There is no way to require the same item.

URL encoding

This parameter must be URL-encoded when sent over HTTP. Most HTTP clients handle this automatically. Examples in this documentation show human-readable syntax for clarity. - applicant.state:CA — nested field filter

When manually constructing URLs, encode these characters:

Example: `` Human-readable: q=status:approved income:>=1000 URL-encoded: q=status%3Aapproved%20income%3A%3E%3D1000 ``

offset integer

Number of items to skip before collecting results.

sort string

Comma-separated list of fields to sort the response by. Prefix a field with - for descending order. The first field is the primary sort; subsequent fields are tie-breakers in declaration order.

More

Examples

  • sort=createdAt — oldest first
  • sort=-createdAt — newest first
  • sort=-priority,dueDate — highest priority first, then oldest due date
  • sort=name.lastName,name.firstName — alphabetical by surname, then given name

Allowed fields

Which fields a given list endpoint allows is declared in the operation's x-sortable.fields extension. Sending a field name not present in that list returns 400 FIELD_NOT_SORTABLE. Sending a field name that doesn't exist on the resource schema returns 400 INVALID_SORT_FIELD. When this parameter is omitted, the operation's x-sortable.default (if declared) is applied; otherwise no client-driven sort is applied. A configured tie-breaker (default id) is always appended for stable pagination.

See api-patterns.yaml#sorting for the full convention and docs/architecture/x-extensions.md for the extension shape.
